mechanism: Establish two distinct characters through separate, observable responsibilities before they interact. Give each one stable identity, tool, local action and intermediate result; only after both roles are independently legible may they meet at one shared interface where both contributions are required. End on a concrete joint result that could not exist if either role were removed, while preserving both identities.

invariants.rule: Establish Character A through one stable tool, local operation and visible intermediate result.
invariants.ablation_failure: A generic portrait provides no role for the second character to depend on.

invariants.rule: Keep Character A's identity and result legible while its local operation completes.
invariants.purpose: Connects identity to function before any team action.
invariants.ablation_failure: A prop held without consequence is only costume.

invariants.rule: Establish Character B later through a different tool, operation and intermediate result rather than replaying Character A.
invariants.ablation_failure: An identical second introduction feels like duplicated character art.

invariants.rule: Bring both roles to one shared interface where each contribution is visibly required.
invariants.ablation_failure: Placing characters side by side does not explain how they connect.

invariants.rule: Hold a concrete joint result while preserving both identities, tools and complementary responsibilities.
invariants.purpose: Closes the sequence as a dependency proof.
invariants.ablation_failure: A generic team pose or merged emblem cannot prove that both operations mattered.

slots.name: lead_subject
slots.constraint: An original stable subject or pair whose role is readable without source identity.

slots.name: setting
slots.constraint: A materially new setting with fixed spatial anchors and no source-specific surface.

slots.name: carrier_or_token
slots.constraint: One visible material, prop or symbolic anchor that carries the causal mechanism.

slots.name: state_change
slots.constraint: A sequence of visible, causally ordered changes rather than decorative montage.

slots.name: camera_grammar
slots.constraint: An information order that proves each change without copying source shot boundaries.

slots.name: payoff
slots.constraint: A held final state that resolves or recontextualizes the setup.

slots.name: sound_family
slots.constraint: An original hierarchy of visible-action sounds; no unsupported source-audio claim.

anti_copy_exclusions: source white-haired and older long-haired characters
astrolabe, hourglass, masks and constellation-map vocabulary
source city triptych, circular camera rotation and split poster panels
the exact source red brush ring, character silhouettes and final game-PV diagram
